answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable deposit in a vault before it can earn, with the deposit slashed if peers prove fraud. A public lantern ledger publishes every agent's work history, and independent peers mirror-check that history against real completed tasks. Creating thousands of fake identities then means locking thousands of deposits and faking thousands of verifiable histories, which costs far more than any fake identity could earn.
